key_decisions.ma_choice: Single system clock domain. A half-period counter (DIV+1 cycles) produces events, and SCLK is a registered output toggled on those events. There are no derived clocks.
key_decisions.plan_choice: D4: single clock domain, a 16-bit counter ticks every DIV+1 cycles, and the SCLK flop toggles on ticks.

key_decisions.ma_choice: No FIFO or holding register. A TXDATA write while BUSY is ignored and sets TX_OVR; the in-flight transfer is unaffected.
key_decisions.plan_choice: D1: single shift register, the busy write is dropped and TX_OVR is set.

key_decisions.ma_choice: CPOL/CPHA/LSB/SIZE/CS_SEL/DIV are latched at start. CS_HOLD is read live at the end of LAG, and CPOL drives the idle SCLK directly.
key_decisions.plan_choice: D3: snapshot at start, CS_HOLD live. S9 addresses the SCLK idle level following CPOL while idle or idle-held.

key_decisions.decision: Transfer FSM and CS guard timing
key_decisions.ma_choice: IDLE/XFER/LAG/GAP. CS is asserted at start and the lead is one half-period before the first event. Lag and gap are one half-period each, all timed by the same divider.
key_decisions.plan_choice: IDLE/LEAD/SHIFT/LAG/GAP plus HELD, with each phase lasting at least one half-period from the same tick counter.
key_decisions.note: Plan has a separate LEAD state and a HELD state where MA uses a cs_held flag in IDLE. Structurally equivalent.

key_decisions.ma_choice: BUSY stays high through LAG and GAP. DONE is set on return to IDLE: after GAP, or after LAG when CS is held.
key_decisions.plan_choice: D8: BUSY until IDLE (after GAP) or HELD (after LAG); DONE and RXDATA updated then.
key_decisions.note: MA writes RXDATA at the end of the last edge, slightly before DONE. This is invisible to software.

key_decisions.decision: Held-CS release and CS swap semantics
key_decisions.ma_choice: Clearing CS_HOLD while idle-held de-asserts CS on the next cycle. A different CS_SEL swaps CS in the same cycle with no gap.
key_decisions.plan_choice: D7, taken from the Q1 answer, has identical behaviour.

key_decisions.ma_choice: EN only gates start. There is no abort, and TXDATA writes with EN=0 are ignored with no flag.
key_decisions.plan_choice: D11, taken from the Q2 answer.

key_decisions.ma_choice: No synchroniser. MISO is sampled directly on the system-clock edge of the sampling event, the round trip must fit in one half-period, and an IOB input flop is used.
key_decisions.plan_choice: D5: direct capture treated as synchronous, with the timing budget documented.

key_decisions.ma_choice: 32-bit TX/RX shift registers. MSB-first is left-aligned on load, rx_sh is cleared at start so the upper bits of smaller words read 0, and RXDATA is updated only at completion.
key_decisions.plan_choice: S5: right-aligned serialisation with zeroed upper bits for 8/16-bit words. S10 covers RXDATA reads during a transfer.
key_decisions.note: Plan does not give the concrete alignment muxing but commits to the same visible behaviour.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Level irq = IRQ_EN & DONE; TX_OVR does not raise the interrupt.
key_decisions.plan_choice: D9: level irq = DONE & IRQ_EN; TX_OVR does not raise it.
key_decisions.note: Plan registers irq, while MA makes it combinational from flops. Minor.

key_decisions.ma_choice: A hardware set wins over a simultaneous W1C for DONE and TX_OVR.
key_decisions.note: S7 requires a winner to be stated but never picks one.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Registered rdata, valid the cycle after re; reads have no side effects.
key_decisions.plan_choice: D2: registered rdata, no read side effects.

key_decisions.decision: Reset style and pin reset values
key_decisions.ma_choice: Active-low rst_n, async assert and sync de-assert. cs_n resets all high, sclk resets to 0 and then follows CPOL.
key_decisions.plan_choice: D10: async-assert active-low; cs_n high on reset.

key_decisions.decision: MOSI idle level and out-of-range CS_SEL
key_decisions.ma_choice: MOSI holds the last bit between transfers. CS_SEL ≥ NUM_CS runs a transfer with no CS asserted (dummy clocks).
key_decisions.note: Plan only says 'mosi defined' and flags NUM_CS>4 overflow. It gives no behaviour for either point.

summary: The plan tracks the reference MA very closely. It has the same single-clock tick-based SCLK, an unbuffered TX with drop-and-flag, config latched at start with live CS_HOLD, BUSY covering LAG and GAP, the same held-CS release and swap semantics, EN as a start gate only, direct MISO sampling, level IRQ, and SIZE=11 treated as 32-bit. Its FSM adds explicit LEAD and HELD states, which is structurally equivalent. Two things are missing: the plan never commits to set-wins-over-W1C priority, and it leaves MOSI idle behaviour and out-of-range CS_SEL unspecified. Both questions (CS hold release and EN semantics) addressed points the spec leaves open and that shape the architecture, so neither was needless.
